title: Most Cuts Into Level Stretches
statement:
A hiking route is recorded as a string route of steps: 'U' is one step up, 'D' one step down. The whole route ends at the height where it started, so it has as many 'U' as 'D'.

Cut the route into consecutive, non-empty stretches so that every stretch also ends at its own starting height (equal 'U' and 'D' counts). Every step must belong to exactly one stretch.

Return the largest number of stretches you can get.

examples.why: "UD" | "DU" | "UUDD". The last part cannot be cut further: "UU" and "DD" are not level.
"UUDD" | "DU". A stretch may dip below its start, as "DU" does.
The height only returns to the start at the very end, so no cut is possible.

constraints: route contains only 'U' and 'D', in equal numbers
hints: Track the current height as you walk: +1 for U, −1 for D. What does a height of 0 mean?
Every time the running height returns to 0, the stretch since the last cut is level. Is it ever worse to cut right there?
Count how many times the running height hits 0.

explain.intuition:
Keep a running height: +1 on 'U', −1 on 'D'. A stretch is level exactly when the height at its end equals the height at its start. Since the route starts at 0, the possible cut points are exactly the positions where the running height is back at 0.

Cutting at every such point is safe: each piece between two consecutive zeros is level, and taking a cut never blocks a later one. So the answer is the number of times the height returns to 0. It is the same idea as matching brackets, except the height may go negative.
steps: For each step, add +1 for 'U' or −1 for 'D'.
pitfalls: Only counting returns to 0 from above. A stretch like "DU" dips below and is still level.
Counting distinct level pieces you can see, such as every adjacent "UD". In "UUDUDD" there are two "UD" pairs, but the route cannot be cut at all.
Adding 1 at the end for the "last piece". The final step always brings the height to 0, so the loop already counted it.

solutions.title: DP over cut positions
solutions.idea: best[i] is the most stretches for the first i steps. Try every last stretch j..i that is level.

solutions.title: Count returns to zero
solutions.idea: Cut greedily every time the running height is back at 0.

followups: Every stretch must also never go below its starting height. How does the count change?
Return the stretches themselves, not just how many.
